questions.question_en: The limit as n → ∞ of the sequence a_n = (1 + 2/n)^(3n) is:
questions.question_hi:
[Sequences & Series of Real Numbers • IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
The limit as n → ∞ of the sequence a_n = (1 + 2/n)^(3n) is:
questions.explanation_en: Using lim_{n→∞} (1 + x/n)^n = e^x, we have lim_{n→∞} [(1 + 2/n)^n]³ = (e²)³ = e⁶.
questions.explanation_hi:

questions.question_en: For which values of the real parameter p does the alternating series Σ_{n=2}^∞ (−1)^n / (n (ln n)^p) converge conditionally?
questions.question_hi:
[Convergence of Infinite Series • IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
For which values of the real parameter p does the alternating series Σ_{n=2}^∞ (−1)^n / (n (ln n)^p) converge conditionally?
questions.explanation_en: By the Alternating Series Test (Leibniz criterion), 1/(n (ln n)^p) decreases monotonically to 0 for all p ≥ 0, so the series converges for p ≥ 0. By the Integral Test, Σ 1/(n (ln n)^p) converges absolutely only for p > 1. Hence it converges conditionally for 0 ≤ p ≤ 1.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
By the Alternating Series Test (Leibniz criterion), 1/(n (ln n)^p) decreases monotonically to 0 for all p ≥ 0, so the series converges for p ≥ 0. By the Integral Test, Σ 1/(n (ln n)^p) converges absolutely only for p > 1. Hence it converges conditionally for 0 ≤ p ≤ 1.

questions.question_en: The number of distinct real roots of the polynomial equation x⁵ − 5x + 2 = 0 in R is:
questions.question_hi:
[Functions of One Real Variable (Rolle's & Mean Value Theorem) • IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
The number of distinct real roots of the polynomial equation x⁵ − 5x + 2 = 0 in R is:
questions.explanation_en: Let f(x) = x⁵ − 5x + 2. Then f'(x) = 5(x⁴ − 1) = 0 at x = −1 and x = 1. Since f(−2) = −20 < 0, f(−1) = 6 > 0, f(1) = −2 < 0, and f(2) = 24 > 0, by the Intermediate Value Theorem and Rolle's Theorem, f(x) has exactly 3 real roots.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
Let f(x) = x⁵ − 5x + 2. Then f'(x) = 5(x⁴ − 1) = 0 at x = −1 and x = 1. Since f(−2) = −20 < 0, f(−1) = 6 > 0, f(1) = −2 < 0, and f(2) = 24 > 0, by the Intermediate Value Theorem and Rolle's Theorem, f(x) has exactly 3 real roots.

questions.question_en: Let F(x) = ∫_0^(x²) cos(√t) dt for x > 0. Then the derivative F'(π) is equal to:
questions.question_hi:
[Riemann Integration & Fundamental Theorem of Calculus • IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
Let F(x) = ∫_0^(x²) cos(√t) dt for x > 0. Then the derivative F'(π) is equal to:
questions.explanation_en: By Leibniz's rule for differentiating under the integral sign, F'(x) = cos(√(x²)) · (2x) = 2x cos(x). Evaluating at x = π gives F'(π) = 2π cos(π) = −2π.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
By Leibniz's rule for differentiating under the integral sign, F'(x) = cos(√(x²)) · (2x) = 2x cos(x). Evaluating at x = π gives F'(π) = 2π cos(π) = −2π.

questions.question_en: The critical point (1, 1) of the smooth function f(x, y) = x³ + y³ − 3xy is a:
questions.question_hi:
[Multivariable Calculus (Maxima & Minima) • IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
The critical point (1, 1) of the smooth function f(x, y) = x³ + y³ − 3xy is a:
questions.explanation_en: ∇f = (3x² − 3y, 3y² − 3x) = (0, 0) at (0, 0) and (1, 1). At (1, 1), f_{xx} = 6 > 0, f_{yy} = 6, f_{xy} = −3, and Hessian determinant D = (6)(6) − (−3)² = 27 > 0. Hence (1, 1) is a strict local minimum with f(1, 1) = 1 + 1 − 3 = −1.
questions.explanation_hi:

∇f = (3x² − 3y, 3y² − 3x) = (0, 0) at (0, 0) and (1, 1). At (1, 1), f_{xx} = 6 > 0, f_{yy} = 6, f_{xy} = −3, and Hessian determinant D = (6)(6) − (−3)² = 27 > 0. Hence (1, 1) is a strict local minimum with f(1, 1) = 1 + 1 − 3 = −1.

Consider the differential equation (y + x³) dx + (a x + b y³) dy = 0. If this equation is exact on R², what is the value of the constant a, and what is the general implicit solution when b = 1?
options_en: a = 1 and x y + x⁴/4 + y⁴/4 = C
a = −1 and xy − x⁴/4 + y⁴/4 = C
options_hi: a = 1 and x y + x⁴/4 + y⁴/4 = C
a = −1 and xy − x⁴/4 + y⁴/4 = C
questions.explanation_en: For exactness, ∂M/∂y = 1 must equal ∂N/∂x = a, so a = 1. Integrating M dx + N dy = (y + x³)dx + (x + y³)dy = 0 yields xy + x⁴/4 + y⁴/4 = C.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
For exactness, ∂M/∂y = 1 must equal ∂N/∂x = a, so a = 1. Integrating M dx + N dy = (y + x³)dx + (x + y³)dy = 0 yields xy + x⁴/4 + y⁴/4 = C.

questions.question_en: The general solution of the homogeneous Cauchy-Euler differential equation x² y'' − 3x y' + 4y = 0 for x > 0 is:
questions.question_hi:
[Differential Equations (Cauchy-Euler Equation) • IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
The general solution of the homogeneous Cauchy-Euler differential equation x² y'' − 3x y' + 4y = 0 for x > 0 is:
questions.explanation_en: Substituting y = x^m gives the indicial equation m(m − 1) − 3m + 4 = m² − 4m + 4 = (m − 2)² = 0, which has a repeated root m = 2. Hence y(x) = (c1 + c2 ln x) x².
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
Substituting y = x^m gives the indicial equation m(m − 1) − 3m + 4 = m² − 4m + 4 = (m − 2)² = 0, which has a repeated root m = 2. Hence y(x) = (c1 + c2 ln x) x².

questions.question_en: Let A be a 3 × 3 real matrix with characteristic polynomial p(λ) = det(λI − A) = λ³ − 6λ² + 11λ − 6. Then the trace of A⁻¹ is:
questions.question_hi:
[Linear Algebra (Cayley-Hamilton & Matrix Inverse) • IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
Let A be a 3 × 3 real matrix with characteristic polynomial p(λ) = det(λI − A) = λ³ − 6λ² + 11λ − 6. Then the trace of A⁻¹ is:
questions.explanation_en: The roots of λ³ − 6λ² + 11λ − 6 = (λ − 1)(λ − 2)(λ − 3) = 0 are the eigenvalues of A: λ = 1, 2, 3. Therefore the eigenvalues of A⁻¹ are 1, 1/2, 1/3, and Trace(A⁻¹) = 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 = 11/6.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
The roots of λ³ − 6λ² + 11λ − 6 = (λ − 1)(λ − 2)(λ − 3) = 0 are the eigenvalues of A: λ = 1, 2, 3. Therefore the eigenvalues of A⁻¹ are 1, 1/2, 1/3, and Trace(A⁻¹) = 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 = 11/6.

questions.question_en: The maximum possible order of an element (permutation) in the symmetric group S_8 is:
questions.question_hi:
[Finite Group Theory (Order of Elements in S_n) • IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
The maximum possible order of an element (permutation) in the symmetric group S_8 is:
questions.explanation_en: The order of a permutation in S_8 is the LCM of its disjoint cycle lengths, which partition 8. Since 8 = 3 + 5 with gcd(3, 5) = 1, LCM(3, 5) = 15 is the maximum possible order (Landau's function g(8) = 15).

questions.question_en: The radius of convergence R of the power series Σ_{n=1}^∞ (n! / n^n) x^n is:

[Power Series Radius of Convergence • IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]

questions.explanation_hi:

questions.question_en: The value of the iterated integral ∫_0^1 [∫_y^1 e^(x²) dx] dy is:
questions.question_hi:
[Double Integrals (Change of Order of Integration) • IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
The value of the iterated integral ∫_0^1 [∫_y^1 e^(x²) dx] dy is:
questions.explanation_en: Reversing the order of integration over 0 ≤ y ≤ x ≤ 1 gives ∫_0^1 [∫_0^x dy] e^(x²) dx = ∫_0^1 x e^(x²) dx = [(1/2) e^(x²)]_0^1 = (e − 1)/2.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):

questions.question_en: If a square matrix A ≠ I satisfies A³ = I over C, which of the following can be its minimal polynomial m_A(x) if A is a real matrix with no real eigenvalues?
questions.question_hi:
[Linear Algebra (Minimal Polynomial) • IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
If a square matrix A ≠ I satisfies A³ = I over C, which of the following can be its minimal polynomial m_A(x) if A is a real matrix with no real eigenvalues?
questions.explanation_en: Since A³ − I = (A − I)(A² + A + I) = 0 and A has no real eigenvalues, (x − 1) cannot divide the minimal polynomial of A. Thus m_A(x) = x² + x + 1.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
Since A³ − I = (A − I)(A² + A + I) = 0 and A has no real eigenvalues, (x − 1) cannot divide the minimal polynomial of A. Thus m_A(x) = x² + x + 1.

questions.question_en: In the cyclic group Z_60 under addition modulo 60, the number of generators of the unique subgroup of order 15 is:

Let f : [0, 1] → R be a continuous function. Which of the following statement(s) is/are ALWAYS true?
options_en: The image f([0, 1]) is a closed and bounded interval [a, b].
f is differentiable at least at one point in (0, 1).
options_hi: The image f([0, 1]) is a closed and bounded interval [a, b].
f is differentiable at least at one point in (0, 1).

questions.question_en: Let A be an n × n real symmetric positive-definite matrix. Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?
questions.question_hi:
[Linear Algebra (Positive Definite Matrices) • IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
Let A be an n × n real symmetric positive-definite matrix. Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?
options_en: All eigenvalues of A are strictly positive.
A² and A⁻¹ are also symmetric positive-definite matrices.
The leading principal minors of A alternate in sign.
options_hi: All eigenvalues of A are strictly positive.
A² and A⁻¹ are also symmetric positive-definite matrices.
The leading principal minors of A alternate in sign.
questions.explanation_en: A real symmetric matrix is positive definite iff all its eigenvalues λ_i > 0, which implies det(A) = Π λ_i > 0, Trace(A) = Σ λ_i > 0, and A², A⁻¹ have positive eigenvalues λ_i² and 1/λ_i. By Sylvester's criterion, all leading principal minors are strictly positive (they alternate in sign for negative definite matrices).
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
A real symmetric matrix is positive definite iff all its eigenvalues λ_i > 0, which implies det(A) = Π λ_i > 0, Trace(A) = Σ λ_i > 0, and A², A⁻¹ have positive eigenvalues λ_i² and 1/λ_i. By Sylvester's criterion, all leading principal minors are strictly positive (they alternate in sign for negative definite matrices).

questions.question_en: Consider f : R² → R defined by f(x, y) = (x y²) / (x² + y⁴) for (x, y) ≠ (0, 0) and f(0, 0) = 0. Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE at the origin (0, 0)?
questions.question_hi:
[Multivariable Calculus (Partial Derivatives & Continuity) • IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
Consider f : R² → R defined by f(x, y) = (x y²) / (x² + y⁴) for (x, y) ≠ (0, 0) and f(0, 0) = 0. Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE at the origin (0, 0)?
options_en: Both partial derivatives ∂f/∂x (0, 0) and ∂f/∂y (0, 0) exist and equal 0.
All directional derivatives D_u f(0, 0) exist along every unit vector u = (a, b).
options_hi: Both partial derivatives ∂f/∂x (0, 0) and ∂f/∂y (0, 0) exist and equal 0.
All directional derivatives D_u f(0, 0) exist along every unit vector u = (a, b).
questions.explanation_en: Along the parabolic path x = y², f(y², y) = y⁴ / (2y⁴) = 1/2 ≠ 0, so f is NOT continuous (and hence not differentiable) at (0, 0). However, along any straight line (t a, t b), f(t a, t b)/t = a b² / (a² + t² b⁴) → b²/a (for a ≠ 0) and 0 (for a = 0), so all directional and partial derivatives exist at (0, 0).
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
Along the parabolic path x = y², f(y², y) = y⁴ / (2y⁴) = 1/2 ≠ 0, so f is NOT continuous (and hence not differentiable) at (0, 0). However, along any straight line (t a, t b), f(t a, t b)/t = a b² / (a² + t² b⁴) → b²/a (for a ≠ 0) and 0 (for a = 0), so all directional and partial derivatives exist at (0, 0).

For the bounded real sequence a_n = (−1)^n (1 + 1/n) + cos(nπ/2), which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?

questions.question_en: Let A be the 4 × 4 matrix where every diagonal entry is 5 and every off-diagonal entry is 2. The largest eigenvalue of A is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Linear Algebra (Sum of Eigenvalues) • IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
Let A be the 4 × 4 matrix where every diagonal entry is 5 and every off-diagonal entry is 2. The largest eigenvalue of A is ________.
questions.explanation_en: We can write A = 3I + 2J, where J is the 4 × 4 all-ones matrix (whose eigenvalues are 4, 0, 0, 0). Therefore, the eigenvalues of A are 3 + 2(4) = 11, and 3, 3, 3. The largest eigenvalue is 11.

questions.question_en: The number of elements of order 12 in the direct product group Z_12 × Z_3 is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Group Theory (Euler Totient & Elements of Order d) • IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
The number of elements of order 12 in the direct product group Z_12 × Z_3 is ________.
questions.explanation_en: An element (a, b) ∈ Z_12 × Z_3 has order lcm(|a|, |b|) = 12. Either |a| = 12 (φ(12)=4 choices) and |b| ∈ {1, 3} (3 choices) giving 4×3 = 12 elements, or |a| = 4 (φ(4)=2 choices) and |b| = 3 (φ(3)=2 choices) giving 2×2 = 4 elements. Total = 12 + 4 = 16.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
An element (a, b) ∈ Z_12 × Z_3 has order lcm(|a|, |b|) = 12. Either |a| = 12 (φ(12)=4 choices) and |b| ∈ {1, 3} (3 choices) giving 4×3 = 12 elements, or |a| = 4 (φ(4)=2 choices) and |b| = 3 (φ(3)=2 choices) giving 2×2 = 4 elements. Total = 12 + 4 = 16.

questions.explanation_en: By the symmetry property ∫_0^a f(x) dx = ∫_0^a f(a − x) dx with a = π/2, I + I = ∫_0^(π/2) 1 dx = π/2 => I = π/4 ≈ 0.7854.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
By the symmetry property ∫_0^a f(x) dx = ∫_0^a f(a − x) dx with a = π/2, I + I = ∫_0^(π/2) 1 dx = π/2 => I = π/4 ≈ 0.7854.

questions.explanation_en: Using the integrating factor e^(2x), (y e^(2x))' = 6 e^(2x) => y(x) = 3 + C e^(−2x). With y(0) = 5, C = 2, so y(x) = 3 + 2 e^(−2x). As x → ∞, y(x) → 3.

questions.question_en: Let C be the boundary of the square [0, 2] × [0, 2] oriented counterclockwise in the xy-plane. By Green's Theorem, the value of the line integral ∮_C (y² dx + 4xy dy) is ________.

Let C be the boundary of the square [0, 2] × [0, 2] oriented counterclockwise in the xy-plane. By Green's Theorem, the value of the line integral ∮_C (y² dx + 4xy dy) is ________.

questions.question_en: The exact sum of the infinite series Σ_{n=1}^∞ (2n + 1) / (n² (n + 1)²) is ________.

The exact sum of the infinite series Σ_{n=1}^∞ (2n + 1) / (n² (n + 1)²) is ________.

questions.question_en: Let A = [[2, 1, 0], [0, 2, 1], [0, 0, 2]] be a 3 × 3 Jordan block. The sum of the algebraic multiplicity and the geometric multiplicity of the eigenvalue λ = 2 is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Linear Algebra (Geometric Multiplicity) • IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
Let A = [[2, 1, 0], [0, 2, 1], [0, 0, 2]] be a 3 × 3 Jordan block. The sum of the algebraic multiplicity and the geometric multiplicity of the eigenvalue λ = 2 is ________.
questions.explanation_en: The characteristic polynomial is (λ − 2)³, so the algebraic multiplicity of λ = 2 is 3. Since Rank(A − 2I) = Rank([[0,1,0],[0,0,1],[0,0,0]]) = 2, the geometric multiplicity is 3 − 2 = 1. Their sum is 3 + 1 = 4.

questions.question_en: If the orthogonal trajectory to the family of parabolas y = c x² passing through the point (√2, 1) intersects the y-axis at (0, y0) with y0 > 0, then y0² is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Differential Equations (Orthogonal Trajectories) • IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
If the orthogonal trajectory to the family of parabolas y = c x² passing through the point (√2, 1) intersects the y-axis at (0, y0) with y0 > 0, then y0² is ________.
questions.explanation_en: For y = c x², dy/dx = 2cx = 2y/x. Replacing dy/dx by −dx/dy gives the orthogonal trajectory ODE: dy/dx = −x/(2y) => 2y dy + x dx = 0 => x² + 2y² = K. Passing through (√2, 1) gives 2 + 2(1)² = 4, so at x = 0, 2 y0² = 4 => y0² = 2.

questions.question_en: In the alternating group A_5 (of order 60), the index [A_5 : H] of a subgroup H isomorphic to the Klein four-group V_4 is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Group Theory (Index of Subgroup) • IIT JAM Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
In the alternating group A_5 (of order 60), the index [A_5 : H] of a subgroup H isomorphic to the Klein four-group V_4 is ________.
questions.explanation_en: By Lagrange's Theorem, the index is [A_5 : H] = |A_5| / |V_4| = 60 / 4 = 15.
